title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.39193v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. translated_title: 面向长时程任务的目标感知动态多智能体协作
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体正越来越多地被用于在无人工干预的情况下完成复杂的长时程任务。为了向任务目标推进，智能体需要在适当的时机执行不同的职责，例如规划与验证。为了了解单个智能体在长时程执行过程中如何管理这些职责，我们开展了一项初步研究。我们的分析表明，验证与任务成功的关联性最强，但验证往往发生得较晚，使得纠错的机会十分有限。我们还发现，随着不同职责的记录在共享上下文中不断累积，与职责相关的信息占比会逐渐下降。这些发现促使我们考察多智能体系统（MAS）能否通过将不同职责分配给拥有独立上下文的智能体来解决上述问题。我们的分析表明，仅靠这种职责分离并不足够：智能体可能会偏离整体目标并重复此前的探索，还可能缺乏必要的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文通过实证分析发现单一LLM智能体在长时程任务中验证时机过晚且共享上下文信息被稀释，而简单的职责分离式多智能体系统仍会偏离目标，据此提出目标感知的动态多智能体协作方法来提升长时程任务的成功率。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically shows that single LLM agents in long-horizon tasks verify too late and suffer from context dilution, and that naive duty-separated multi-agent systems still lose track of the overall goal, motivating a goal-aware dynamic multi-agent collaboration approach to improve task success.
